title: The Bench Link: A Controller and a Plant Emulator Exchanging Frames, and What Each Does When the Other Goes Quiet

questions.question: A plant emulator is sent one command of 6 and then nothing for a second. What should it do?
options: Hold it for a moment and then act on zero: with no watchdog it ran at speed 12 to position 10.920, with one it stopped at 0.720
Hold the command for the whole second: with no watchdog it reached position 0.720, the right place
Stop at once, the moment one tick passes with no command: it stopped at 0.060
Repeat the last command at half strength until a new one comes: it reached 5.460
questions.explanation: Holding for a tick or two covers an ordinary gap. Holding for a second is a motor running with nobody in control, so after a few ticks the plant acts on zero.

questions.question: Commands 2 and then 1 arrive, in that order. What does the emulator do with 1?
options: Acts on it, since it arrived last and so is the newest
Ignores it and counts it: it was sent before 2 and was overtaken, and acting on it would undo the newest decision
Queues it and acts on it after command 2 has finished
Averages it with command 2
questions.explanation: The sequence number says 1 was sent first and was overtaken on the way. Acting on it would replace the controller's latest decision with an older one.

questions.question: The link dies for a second just after the target is stepped to -1. Where does a plant that holds its last command end up, against one with a watchdog?
options: -1.45 against -21.85: the watchdog made it worse
-21.85 against -1.45: the held command was the strongest one, run for a second at full speed
-1.00 for both: the plant stops at the target
0.00 for both: the plant returns to where it started
questions.explanation: The last command before the link died was the full push toward the new target. Held for a second, it drove the plant twenty times too far.

questions.question: Measurements with ticks 5, 7, 6, 7 reach the controller. What is kept?
options: All four: every measurement is information
Only 5: anything after the first is a repeat
5 and 7: 6 was overtaken and the second 7 was a repeat, so 2 were refused
5, 7 and 6: only the second 7 is refused
questions.explanation: The emulator's tick orders the measurements. One that is older than the newest already seen, or the same, is refused and counted.

questions.question: At 40 percent loss each way the loop still settled. Why?
options: Each command is built from the latest measurement and a lost one is replaced by the next
The plant is too slow to notice a lost command
The link resends what was lost
Loss of 40 percent each way cancels out over a round trip
questions.explanation: 115 of 300 ticks held a measurement that was not new and the error was still under a thousandth. A lost command or measurement is superseded by the next one a tick later. That is why a stream like this is sent once and not resent.

questions.question: Frames overtook each other 69 times. How much did a controller that took each as it arrived suffer?
options: A great deal: the loop was unstable, 1.6110 against 0.1604
Nothing at all: the order of measurements cannot matter
It settled faster by 2.42 ticks
Little in this loop, 0.1611 against 0.1604, and acted on information 2.42 ticks old against 2.17
questions.explanation: The harm would show in a velocity estimate more than in a proportional gain. A proportional loop barely notices. Anything that differences successive measurements, a velocity or an estimator, would be hurt by taking them out of order.
